title: I created a couple of game and would love your feedback
author: conditionnerd
selftext:
Both games were my original ideas but I used Claude to help code them. 

it's called Seven Suns and it's free to play.

[https://ecastro.itch.io/seven-suns](https://ecastro.itch.io/seven-suns)

  
Seven Suns is a solo push-your-luck voyage into the deep dark.

Every jump takes your ship further from Earth and burns more of the fuel you need to get back. Survey strange worlds for Data, name the Wonders you find, and keep your crew alive. Then make the call, turn after turn: one more star, or home while you still can? Get home and your Data is your score. Run dry and you're Lost in the Dark.

Most voyages take 5 to 15 minutes.

  
I would love your thoughts and I wonder if you think it's worth me adding it to the App Store for a few bucks.

I also created Polyduel

**PolyDuel**

[**https://ecastro.itch.io/polyduel**](https://ecastro.itch.io/polyduel)

**Two duelists. Four dice each. One last-chance D20**.

PolyDuel is a fast dice duel of bluffing and timing. Both players secretly pick a die, reveal, and roll: attack higher than the defense and the difference is damage. Every die you use is spent until the round ends, so the real game is deciding **when** to throw your big dice and when to hold them back.

Play the computer, a friend on the same device, or anyone online. Then take on the campaign: eight voiced bosses, branching roads, relics, and a new daily run every day.

comments.author: BIGCHUG1404
comments.body:
Hi stranger! It’s kind of a right of passage that new AI devs go through where they see what AI can do and they get really excited. When you go online with that excitement, people then do 1 of 2 things: either yell at you and insult you, or try and teach you.

There are some obvious “tells” that are a dead giveaway that a game was the result of a  prompt (and likely wasn’t handled by a human at all during creation beyond the initial prompt). AI has some stock colors, fonts, and art styles that it will default to if you didn’t give it adequate art direction/reference. Also the UI won’t feel “human” if that makes sense. These elements stick out like a sore thumb and are extremely obvious which usually means the game was a 1-prompt exercise and qualifies as “AI slop”. 

Your game unfortunately has those markers. I hope that you don’t get discouraged from this feedback and that you continue to make and develop games. Good luck out there!

replies.author: conditionnerd
replies.body: Thanks! I really appreciate your feedback. I totally get what you're saying. My initial thoughts for both games were a physical board game. I asked Claude to create a digital version of the game with all of the rules and I expanded on my ideas from there. Obviously, I'm not charging for the games and I genuinely think they're fun and just thought I'd share. Thanks again for taking the time to let me know the game clearly has AI genetic markers. I'm glad I didn't try to make it seem like I programmed it myself.

comments.author: hard_farter
comments.body:
Both of these have WAY TOO GOD DAMN MUCH going on from the instant you load the game

good grief, there's like 79 buttons

edit:

dice land here. this is 100000% unnecessary. wherever dice are going to land on a UI should be intuitively designed so you don't need weird useless text on the screen.

my "tutorial mission":
find a wonder. complete it and get home from distance 3 or further for +8 data.

what gives "distance" ? what do I care about gaining +8 data?! 

I think "hmm, maybe I should click the RULES button. So I do.

I'm greeted with an absolutely oppressive wall of text. Oh goodie.

replies.author: conditionnerd
replies.body:
![gif](giphy|kC8N6DPOkbqWTxkNTe)

I agree. I need to consolidate the buttons into something more visually appealing. Thanks for the feedback.

replies.author: hard_farter
replies.body:
I've put more feedback in.

there's just problems, brother. consider how complicated a game like Balatro can be, and how little it really has to tell you straight out of the gate.

I don't know what this game is supposed to be closest to, but you should do some studying on whatever it might be in order to understand where the design is going off the rails, because it feels like I have to probably get a degree in *this game* in order to effectively play it, which means your audience is going to be limited heavily by that.

replies.author: conditionnerd
replies.body: I get it. I didn't expect to post it here and get glowing remarks. This is exactly what I was hoping for. Brutal honesty. Thanks!

replies.author: hard_farter
replies.body:
further in, during a tutorial mission I'm given the option to choose an upgrade that "makes the ion storm count for 1 less"

I don't even know what the ion storm is, how often such a thing occurs, if it's something I need to worry about generally or if it's super important, so how on earth do I know if this is something I should consider?

replies.author: conditionnerd
replies.body: The further out you travel the Ion Storm begins to approach making it riskier to get back to earth. But the further you go, the more data you can collect to improve your score.

replies.author: hard_farter
replies.body: Okay, but the question I'm asking is without reading through that huge rules page and committing it to memory (or having to go back and refer to it constantly), what are the ways that this is communicated to the player?

replies.author: conditionnerd
replies.body: The first time you encounter an ion storm a one time tip pops up explaining it. I wanted to make it a surprise and give the explorer an “oh shit” moment.

replies.author: conditionnerd
replies.body: I took your advice and made some changes. Thanks again

comments.author: NotSuddenBegonia
